source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Steering, p.9-3

procedures.title: Steering gear: adjust
steps: If the preload reading is outside the limits in the specifications at the rear of the manual, adjust the gear.
Loosen the worm bearing adjuster locknut and turn the adjuster (see figure 4 in the manual) until worm end play is just gone.
Check the pull at the wheel and readjust as needed; tighten the locknut and check the pull again.
If the gear feels lumpy after the worm bearing adjustment, the bearings are probably damaged; disassemble the gear and replace the damaged parts.
With the worm set and all mounting bolts tight, turn the wheel gently stop to stop, counting the total turns, then return it exactly halfway to center.
Turn the lash adjuster screw clockwise to remove all gear-tooth lash and tighten the locknut.
Check the pull at the wheel, taking the highest reading as the wheel passes through center; compare with the sector lash spec at the rear of the manual and readjust if needed.
If the maximum is exceeded, back the adjuster out counterclockwise, then come back up to the setting turning clockwise.
Tighten the locknut and recheck that the pull is within the specified range.
Refit the pitman arm to the sector shaft on the marks made at removal and torque it to the spec at the rear of the manual.
Refit the horn cap or shroud and reconnect the column harness at the chassis connector.
